name: Washington
overview: Washington provides county-income-tiered senior/disability property-tax exemptions and repayable deferrals; these are distinct from refundable renter credits.

programs.name: Senior Citizen and Disabled Persons Property Tax Exemption
programs.ageRule: At least 61, retired due to disability, or qualifying disabled veteran under the 2025 rules.
programs.incomeDefinition: Combined disposable income after authorized exclusions and deductions.
programs.incomeLimits: County-specific income thresholds for tax years 2024–2026.
programs.maximumBenefit: Varies by income tier, home value and local levy rates.
programs.formulaSummary: Exempts designated levies and portions of assessed value, with assessment-freeze provisions.
programs.application: Apply to county assessor; periodic renewal and change reporting required.
eligibilityNotes: Veteran qualification changed in later legislation; use the 2025 rule.

programs.name: Senior Citizen and Disabled Persons Property Tax Deferral
programs.ageRule: 60 or older, or retired due to disability.
programs.maximumBenefit: Eligible current and delinquent taxes and assessments, subject to equity.
programs.formulaSummary: State-paid taxes accrue 5% simple interest and must be repaid after specified events.

sources.title: Washington Property Tax Exemptions and Deferrals

programs.name: Property Tax Deferral for Homeowners with Limited Income
programs.formulaSummary: Repayable deferral with variable simple interest tied to the federal short-term rate plus two percentage points.
programs.application: Apply through county assessor by September 1; annual renewal.
eligibilityNotes: Five years of homeownership, primary residence and sufficient equity.

sources.title: Washington Property Tax Exemptions and Deferrals

laterChanges: 2026 legislation changes eligibility and thresholds for later tax years; 2027–2029 schedules must not replace the 2024–2026 schedule.
researchNotes: A 2025 exemption amount needs county, assessment and levy details; household income and a total tax bill alone are insufficient.
No statewide refundable residential property-tax or renter credit was identified in the official relief sources reviewed; this is not a claim that Washington provides no property-tax relief.
